approved: Defence and Veterans’ Service Commissioner Bill 2025
Written by a model from the Bills Digest; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would establish an independent Defence and Veterans’ Service Commissioner under a new standalone act.
The Commissioner could investigate systemic issues related to veteran suicide prevention and wellbeing, and report publicly to the Minister and Parliament.
The Commissioner would not be allowed to make findings of civil or criminal wrongdoing, determine the manner or cause of a veteran’s death, or investigate a single use of a power or duty.
Establish the Defence and Veterans’ Service Commissioner as an independent office under its own legislation.
Repeal Part VIIIE of the Defence Act.
Expand the Commissioner’s functions to cover veterans’ families.
Strengthen the Commissioner’s independence from direction on inquiries.
Allow the Commission to include Deputy Commissioners, Assistant Commissioners, contractors, consultants and other helpers.
Enable the Commissioner to start inquiries on their own initiative into suicide prevention or veteran wellbeing.
Veterans, their families, and Australian Defence Force members would be affected by the Commissioner’s inquiries and reports.

The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2026-02-11.110.1) Herbert MP [Phillip Thompson](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/herbert/phillip_thompson) (LNP), which means it was unsuccessful. Mr Thompson [explained that](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2026-02-11.110.1): > *The coalition is moving an amendment to bring forward the timing of the first implementation review by the commissioner. As currently drafted, the first assessment of the government's implementation of the royal commission recommendations is not required to be completed until December 2027. That means the report may not be tabled until 2028, almost four years after the royal commission reported. That is too slow and risks weakening accountability.* ### Amendment text > *(1) Clause 18, page 20 (line 11), omit "2 December 2027", substitute "30 September 2026".*

Moved the second reading of consequential legislation supporting the Defence and Veterans' Service Commissioner Bill 2025, including amendments to the Archives Act 1983 and the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security Act 1986.

Supported the Defence and Veterans' Service Commissioner bills, arguing that independent oversight, information-gathering powers, public reporting and parliamentary accountability were necessary to drive sustained reform following the Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide; said the commission had been operating since the end of September last year.

Moved procedural motions to expedite consideration of legislation and limit debate, then criticised the government for scheduling 22 bills for rapid passage and alleged that the process lacked transparency and scrutiny.

Argued that the Defence and Veterans' Service Commissioner bills implement a royal commission recommendation for independent oversight, and supported them while seeking stronger independence, powers, transparency and earlier reporting for veterans and their families.
